thread:
eva: Heads-up — I sketched a lightweight proposal for model intake gating. TL;DR: split into a fast pre-admit smoke + async full bench, keep a small deterministic compatibility check during admit.

sam: Curious — what do you mean by deterministic compatibility check?

eva: It runs < 30s, verifies: tokenizer/embedding dims, op kernels used, expected kvcache shape, and that export artifacts load in runtime with a minimal forward pass. No perf numbers. Basically a "will it run on the runtime" gate.

jin: Love that. My worry: teams will rely on the async bench too little if admit is fast. We need a clear SLO for async results to land.

marcos: I sketched tradeoffs:
- Full bench in admit = slow onboarding, fewer blurry uploads, earlier regressions caught.
- Async bench = fast flow, but risk of model drifting into prod before bench finishes.

eva: Right. Proposed compromise: admit = smoke + deterministic compatibility + a simple quality check (small handful of eval prompts w/ golden outputs). Async = full benchmark (latency P50/P95, memory, kv rate, throughput, quantization compatibility).

sam: For "golden outputs" we need guardrails. Do we store prompt+expected hash per model family? How do we handle nondeterministic models?

jin: Use short deterministic prompts (sampling=0, fixed seed) for admit hashes. If model uses sampling layers that are non-deterministic even with seed, mark family as "probabilistic" and require additional checklist (eval threshold) in async.

marcos: Operational question: what happens if async bench fails after admit? Do we automatically retract? or put into quarantine?

eva: My suggestion: auto-quarantine (no traffic) + notify owners and platform. Don’t auto-retract if model already served customer traffic — instead create a mitigation plan: rollback routes, pin older model, or reduce traffic via routing policy.

infra-bot: Deploy-checker: note recorded — add "quarantine" state to model registry with reason codes (compat, perf, quality).

qa-bot: Also add retention for async bench artifacts (bench logs, perf traces, sample outputs) for 30d by default. Helps for root-cause.

sam: Another tradeoff: where to run async bench? Dedicated infra vs shared ephemeral infra. Dedicated gives deterministic perf but higher cost. Shared is cheaper but noisy.

marcos: We already have a cheap ephemeral bench pool for initial runs. Proposal: ephemeral pool for first async run; if perf is borderline or quantization hint found, re-run on dedicated cluster (auto escalation).

jin: Sounds good. What signals trigger escalation? P95 > threshold OR memory > x% OR quantization failure OR unknown ops reported.

eva: I'll add specific numbers in the doc, e.g., P95 threshold per model class: small 50ms, medium 120ms, large 500ms (placeholder). Also add rule: any unknown op in graph => immediate dedicated run.

sam: Compatibility check details: we should compute a deterministic fingerprint of the model graph + aten ops list + layernorm types. That helps detect operator-level regressions across versions.

marcos: Add to that: compute an export hash + runtime-consume hash (after loading) to handle cases where exporter rewrites things.

eva: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with a checklist: admit-smoke -> compatibility fingerprint -> golden-hash -> create async bench job -> run on ephemeral -> escalate if signals -> mark results in registry + artifacts.

jin: Action: eva to post RFC follow-up with the concrete thresholds and the new registry states. marcos to outline escalation infra. sam to add deterministic prompt set and seeding doc. All: quick thumbs up in thread when you can.

marcos: OK will start infra outline tomorrow.

sam: I'll put together 20 deterministic prompts across families.

eva: Thanks. If no objections by EOD we'll ship the follow-up draft. :rocket:

jin: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: note: model-registry schema update suggested: add field "admit_checks" (list) and "async_bench_id" (string).
